newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico gov't sees 20,000 T avocado exports to U.S..
newsitem.headline: Mexico gov't sees 20,000 T avocado exports to U.S..

text.p: Mexican Agriculture Minister Francisco Labastida Ochoa said he believed the country will export 20,000 tonnes of avocadoes to the United States in the next November-February export period that has opened up for national growers.

In a statement Tuesday, Labastida said his estimate was based on the probability that there would be 2,000 hectares of certified avocado growing regions by November. He said with a $3 per kilo price it would mean $60 million in export revenues.
The U.S. government relaxed a 83-year ban on Mexican avocadoes last Friday, allowing exports to 19 states between November and February each winter.
Other limitations on exports are that they have to originate from the central state of Michoacan, and from certified counties and farms and must be the Hass variety.
Currently, only 500 hectares are recognised by the U.S. Agriculture Department.

"But a viable goal, perhaps a little conservative, is to increase that surface area to 2,000 hectares for when the market opens in November and thereafter reach 12,000 hectares growing export-quality avocadoes," Labastida said.
Avocado growers are a little more conservative on their predictions for exports this first November-February period.
Enrique Batista, the head of the Michoacan Avocado Committee, estimated just 5,000 tonnes will be sent to the U.S. over the coming winter.

He cited the limited current market -- only around 25,000 tonnes of avocadoes are consumed in the 19 states in the three month period -- and also transportation difficulties, because the market os far from Michoacan.
((--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com))
